item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is preferable for its more focused scope and stronger coverage of the reported configuration, though both patches violate a central contract requirement by duplicating FilesService.Add instead of routing Upload through it.","reasons":["B’s retry test explicitly enables RetryAllMethods, matching the reported POST-upload scenario; A’s retry test omits it.","B tests both required pre-request validation cases and verifies no request is made. A implements validation but does not test it.","B directly verifies the multipart media type, field name, filename, and content.","B avoids unrelated README/CHANGELOG churn and A’s test that codifies existing non-replayable Add behavior rather than verifying the new API contract."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add’s option handling, request execution, decoding, and error handling instead of calling Add.","No tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures.","The retry test uses strings.Reader and omits RetryAllMethods, so it does not closely model the reported streamed os.File POST case."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add’s implementation instead of routing the encoded body through Add, violating the frozen contract and risking future semantic drift.","No test covers propagation of source-reader failures.","The retry test supplies bytes.Reader rather than a non-replayable streamed source, so it does not prove that buffering fixes the original reader type independently of the helper’s known behavior."]}
